We have life expectancy dataset too big. We need criteria:

1. Population >10 million in 1950. So need countries with population >10m in 1950.

2. Deaths from armed conflicts on territory <100 from 1989-2023 (total best estimate). So need a dataset of cumulative deaths 1989-2023. Our world has deaths-in-armored conflicts API: deaths-in-armed-conflicts is cumulative but might be per year? The link "deaths-in-armed-conflicts.csv" likely has yearly data. We need cumulative sum 1989-2023.

We also need total emigrants <1 million in 2020. Data likely in "emigration" dataset: "Net migration to population" or "emigrants" dataset. Our world has "Net migration" but also dataset "Net migration (per 1000)" etc. We need total number of emigrants, perhaps "Emigration" dataset.

## What you should know about this indicator

*   The UN defines an international migrant as someone who has been living for one year or longer in a country other than their country of birth.
*   This chart shows the total number of emigrants in each country. For example, if you are looking at the United States, the number of emigrants is the number of people who were born in the United States but now live in another country.
*   For the majority of countries the UN defines immigrants or emigrants on the basis of country of birth. Someone who lives in a country other than the one in which they were born is considered an immigrant, even if they have acquired citizenship of the country in which they live. For countries where data on place of birth is not available, the UN uses citizenship instead.

#### United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs – International Migrant Stock

The 2024 edition of the International Migrant Stock dataset presents the latest United Nations estimates of the numbers and characteristics of international migrants around the world. Covering the period from 1990 to 2024, the dataset includes estimates of the total number of international migrants by sex, as well as their places of origin and destination, for 233 countries and areas.

In producing the 2024 edition of the International Migrant Stock dataset, the Population Division has prioritized revising the estimates for countries with new empirical information from population censuses or registers and relatively large numbers of international migrants, as well as for countries affected by ongoing or emergent refugee flows as documented by UNHCR. In the new edition of these data, a total of 60 countries and areas received a full reassessment of trends in the number of international migrants residing in the territory. For the remaining countries and areas, the estimates generated in 2024 reflect extrapolations of estimates published in the 2020 edition of the dataset.

steps.text:
Maybe cohort dataset is not directly, but we can approximate by using life expectancy at birth in 1958 as period value? But question: "which had the closest life expectancy at birth to Australia, for people born in 1958?" That implies cohort life expectancy for birth cohort 1958. Our dataset we have is period life expectancy. Could we approximate cohort from period for same year? Not exact.

But maybe we can use "life expectancy at birth" for year 1958; for each country we will find the 1958 value. For Australia 1958 value is 70.8606 (from period). That is used as reference. The question: "closest life expectancy at birth to Australia, for people born in 1958?" So we use period life expectancy value for each country in 1958 to compare.

Thus we need to extract for all countries that satisfy criteria: population >10M in 1950; armed conflict deaths <100 (best estimate) from 1989-2023; and emigrants <1M in 2020. Then select among them the country whose life expectancy in 1958 is closest to Australia value 70.8606.

We need to find dataset for population 1950.

Our population csv from earlier has population in all years. We'll need 1950 population for each country.

Our armed conflict deaths dataset: Let's fetch. Search.

steps.text:
CSV contains cumulative deaths worldwide, not per year exactly. But includes per year. We need 1989-2023 cumulative. Might use 2023 value, but dataset has 2024. We could maybe approximate by 2023 value by subtracting 2024 incremental? But the dataset gives 2024 fig, not enough.

Alternatively, could use deaths-in-armed-conflicts dataset (annual deaths). Then sum from 1989 to 2023 to get cumulative. But that's effort.

We can check source data for "deaths-in-armed-conflicts.csv".
